question: Fill the blank with ⊂ or ⊄: {x : x is a student of Class XI of your school} ... {x : x is a student of your school}
solution: ⊂ — every student of Class XI in the school is automatically a student of the school, so the first set is wholly contained in the second.

question: Let A = {1, 2, {3, 4}, 5}. State which of these are incorrect and why: (i) {3,4} ⊂ A (ii) {3,4} ∈ A (iii) 1 ∈ A (iv) φ ⊂ A
solution: (i) is INCORRECT: {3,4} is itself a single element of A (A has the element {3,4}, not the elements 3 and 4 separately), so it cannot be a subset using ⊂ in that sense — correct relation is {3,4} ∈ A. (ii) is CORRECT: {3,4} literally appears as one of A's elements. (iii) is CORRECT: 1 is listed as an element of A. (iv) is CORRECT: φ is a subset of every set.
steps: A's elements are: 1, 2, the set {3,4}, and 5 — four elements total
{3,4} ∈ A is right since {3,4} is literally one element
{3,4} ⊂ A would need 3 ∈ A and 4 ∈ A individually — false

question: If A={3,5,7,9,11}, B={7,9,11,13}, C={11,13,15}, D={15,17}, find (i) A∩B (ii) B∩C (iii) A∩C∩D
solution: (i) A∩B = {7,9,11} (common to both). (ii) B∩C = {11,13} (common to both). (iii) A∩C∩D: A∩C = {11}; {11}∩D = φ since 11 ∉ D = {15,17}. So A∩C∩D = φ.
steps: A∩B: elements in both A and B → {7,9,11}
B∩C: elements in both B and C → {11,13}
A∩C = {11}, then intersect with D={15,17} → no common element → φ

question: Let U={1,...,9}, A={1,2,3,4}, B={2,4,6,8}, C={3,4,5,6}. Find (i) A′ (ii) (A∪C)′ (iii) (A′)′
solution: (i) A′ = U − A = {5,6,7,8,9}. (ii) A∪C = {1,2,3,4,5,6}, so (A∪C)′ = {7,8,9}. (iii) (A′)′ = A (double complement returns the original set) = {1,2,3,4}.
steps: A′ = everything in U not in A
A∪C first, then take complement of that union

question: Decide which of these sets are subsets of one another: A = {x ∈ R : x² − 8x + 12 = 0}, B = {2,4,6}, C = {2,4,6,8,...}, D = {6}.
solution: Solve x²−8x+12=0: (x−2)(x−6)=0, so x=2 or x=6, giving A = {2,6}. Now D={6} ⊂ A since 6∈A; D ⊂ B since 6∈B; D ⊂ C since 6∈C. Also A ⊂ B (both 2,6 ∈ B) and A ⊂ C (both 2,6 ∈ C, the even numbers). And B ⊂ C (2,4,6 are all even numbers in C). So D ⊂ A ⊂ B ⊂ C.
steps: Solve the quadratic to find A = {2, 6}
Check each small set against the larger ones for containment

question: If A = {−1, 1}, find A × A × A.
steps: Each of the 3 positions can independently be −1 or 1
List systematically to avoid missing/duplicating any

question: Let A = {1,2} and B = {3,4}. Write A × B and find how many subsets it has.
solution: A × B = {(1,3), (1,4), (2,3), (2,4)} — 4 ordered pairs. A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets, so A×B (with 4 elements) has 2⁴ = 16 subsets, ranging from φ to the full set A×B itself.
steps: List all 4 ordered pairs of A×B

question: Let R = {(x, x³) : x is a prime number less than 10}. Write R in roster form.
Find the domain and range of the function f(x) = x²/(1+x²).
solution: Domain: the denominator 1+x² is always ≥1>0 for real x, so f is defined for all real x — domain = R. Range: let y = x²/(1+x²). Since x²≥0, y≥0 always; as x²→∞, y→1 but never reaches 1 (since x² < 1+x² strictly); at x=0, y=0. So range = [0, 1).
steps: Denominator 1+x² is never zero → domain = R
As x² grows, y approaches but never equals 1 → range = [0,1)

question: The function f is defined by f(x) = 1−x for x<0, 1 for x=0, x+1 for x>0. Draw the graph (describe) and find the range.
solution: This is a piecewise function: for x<0, f(x)=1−x which is a line of slope −1 passing through (0,1) but only drawn for x<0 (values >1 there); at x=0, f(0)=1 (a single point); for x>0, f(x)=x+1, a line of slope 1 starting just above (0,1). Checking output values: as x→0⁻, f→1 from above; at x=0, f=1; as x→0⁺, f→1 from above. So the range is [1, ∞) — f(x) ≥ 1 for all x, with equality only at x=0.
steps: Evaluate each piece separately for x<0, x=0, x>0
All three pieces give f(x) ≥ 1 → range = [1, ∞)

question: Find the radian measure of 40° 20′.
steps: Convert minutes to a decimal/fractional degree: 20′ = 1/3°
Multiply by π/180 to convert to radians: 121π/540

question: Find the degree measure corresponding to the radian measure 7π/6.
Prove that cos(3π/2 + x)cos(2π + x)[cot(3π/2 − x) + cot(2π + x)] = 1.
solution: Use standard identities: cos(3π/2+x) = sin x; cos(2π+x) = cos x; cot(3π/2−x) = tan x; cot(2π+x) = cot x. Substituting: sin x · cos x · [tan x + cot x] = sin x cos x × [(sinx/cosx) + (cosx/sinx)] = sin x cos x × [(sin²x+cos²x)/(sinx cosx)] = sin x cos x × [1/(sinx cosx)] = 1.
steps: Reduce each factor using standard angle-shift identities
tan x + cot x combines to 1/(sinx cosx) via sin²+cos²=1
The sinx cosx factors cancel, leaving exactly 1

question: Find the general solution of sin 2x − sin 4x + sin 6x = 0.
solution: Group sin2x+sin6x using sum-to-product: sin2x+sin6x = 2 sin4x cos2x. So the equation becomes 2sin4x cos2x − sin4x = 0, i.e. sin4x(2cos2x − 1) = 0. So either sin4x = 0, giving 4x = nπ, x = nπ/4; or cos2x = 1/2, giving 2x = 2nπ ± π/3, x = nπ ± π/6, for n ∈ Z.
steps: Pair sin2x and sin6x using sum-to-product (equal spacing around 4x)
Solve each factor = 0 separately for the two families of solutions

question: Express (5i)(−3i/5) in the form a + ib.
Find the modulus and argument of z = −1 − i.
solution: Modulus |z| = √((−1)²+(−1)²) = √2. The point (−1,−1) lies in the third quadrant; reference angle is π/4, so the argument is −(π − π/4) = −3π/4 (principal value in (−π, π]).
steps: Point (−1,−1) is in the third quadrant

question: Solve 3x² − 4x + 20/3 = 0 using the quadratic formula.
solution: Multiply through by 3 to clear the fraction: 9x² − 12x + 20 = 0. Discriminant = (−12)² − 4(9)(20) = 144 − 720 = −576. √(−576) = 24i. x = [12 ± 24i]/18 = (2 ± 4i)/3.
steps: Clear the fraction by multiplying the whole equation by 3

question: Evaluate [i^18 + (1/i)^25]^3.
steps: Reduce i^18 and (1/i)^25 using the i-cycle (period 4)
Cube (−1−i): square first to get 2i, then multiply by (−1−i) again to get 2−2i

question: Solve 3(x − 1) ≤ 2(x − 3), and show the solution on a number line.
solution: 3x − 3 ≤ 2x − 6 ⟹ 3x − 2x ≤ −6+3 ⟹ x ≤ −3. Number line: a closed (filled) circle at −3 with shading extending to the left.
steps: Closed circle at −3 (≤ includes the endpoint), shade left

question: A solution is to be kept between 68°F and 77°F. The conversion formula is C = 5/9(F−32). Find the range in Celsius.
solution: 68 < F < 77. Substituting F = 9C/5+32: 68 < 9C/5+32 < 77 ⟹ 36 < 9C/5 < 45 ⟹ 36×5/9 < C < 45×5/9 ⟹ 20 < C < 25. So the temperature range in Celsius is between 20°C and 25°C.
steps: Substitute F in terms of C and simplify the compound inequality

question: How many 4-letter codes can be formed using the first 10 letters of the English alphabet, if no letter can be repeated?
solution: This is a permutation of 10 letters taken 4 at a time: P(10,4) = 10×9×8×7 = 5040.
steps: Order matters (a code), no repetition → permutation

question: In how many ways can a team of 3 boys and 3 girls be selected from 5 boys and 4 girls?
solution: Choose 3 boys from 5: C(5,3) = 10. Choose 3 girls from 4: C(4,3) = 4. By the multiplication principle, total ways = 10 × 4 = 40.

question: In how many ways can one select a cricket team of 11 players from 17 players in which only 5 players can bowl, if each team requires exactly 4 bowlers?
solution: Choose 4 bowlers from the 5 available: C(5,4) = 5. The remaining 7 team spots come from the other 12 non-designated-bowler players (17−5=12): C(12,7) = 792. Total = 5 × 792 = 3960.
steps: Split the 17 players into 5 bowlers and 12 others
Choose 4 of the 5 bowlers, and 7 of the remaining 12 to fill the team

question: Find the 4th term in the expansion of (x − 2y)^12.
Show that 9^(n+1) − 8n − 9 is divisible by 64, whenever n is a positive integer.
solution: Write 9^(n+1) = (1+8)^(n+1). By the binomial theorem, (1+8)^(n+1) = Σ (n+1)Ck · 8^k for k=0 to n+1 = 1 + (n+1)(8) + [terms with k≥2, each containing 8² = 64 as a factor]. So 9^(n+1) = 1 + 8(n+1) + 64M for some integer M (the sum of the remaining terms). Then 9^(n+1) − 8n − 9 = 1 + 8n + 8 + 64M − 8n − 9 = 64M, which is clearly divisible by 64.
steps: The k=0 and k=1 terms give 1 + 8(n+1); every k≥2 term has a factor of 8²=64
Subtracting 8n+9 leaves exactly the multiple-of-64 remainder

question: Find the 20th and nth term of the GP 5/2, 5/4, 5/8, ... .
steps: a = 5/2, r = 1/2 (each term is half the previous)

question: Find the sum to n terms of the series whose nth term is given by n(n+2).
steps: Apply standard formulas Σn² and Σn separately
Combine over a common denominator: n(n+1)(2n+7)/6

question: If AM and GM of two positive numbers a and b are 10 and 8 respectively, find the numbers.
solution: AM = (a+b)/2 = 10 ⟹ a+b = 20. GM = √(ab) = 8 ⟹ ab = 64. a and b are roots of x² − 20x + 64 = 0. Discriminant = 400−256=144, √144=12. x = (20±12)/2 = 16 or 4. So the numbers are 16 and 4.
steps: a+b=20 and ab=64 from the AM and GM conditions

question: Find the slope of the line passing through the points (3, −2) and (−1, 4).
Find the equation of the line passing through (0,0) with slope m.
solution: Using point-slope form through the origin: y − 0 = m(x − 0), i.e. y = mx.

question: Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x − 4y + 7 = 0 and 3x − 4y + 5 = 0.
solution: For parallel lines Ax+By+C1=0 and Ax+By+C2=0, distance = |C1−C2|/√(A²+B²) = |7−5|/√(9+16) = 2/5.
steps: Confirm both lines have the same A,B (parallel) — here A=3,B=−4 for both

question: Find the equation of the circle with centre (−2,3) and radius 4.
Find the coordinates of the focus, axis, equation of directrix, and length of latus rectum for y² = 8x.
solution: Comparing to y²=4ax: 4a=8, so a=2. Focus = (a,0) = (2,0). Axis = x-axis (the line y=0). Directrix: x=−a, i.e. x=−2. Length of latus rectum = 4a = 8.

question: Find the equation of the ellipse with foci (±3,0) and vertices (±5,0).
solution: Vertices at (±5,0) means a=5. Foci at (±3,0) means c=3. Using b²=a²−c² = 25−9=16. Equation: x²/25 + y²/16 = 1.

question: Find the distance between the points (2,3,5) and (4,3,1).
steps: Subtract corresponding coordinates: Δx=2, Δy=0, Δz=−4

question: Find the coordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining (−2,3,5) and (1,−4,6) in the ratio 2:3 internally.
steps: Apply the section formula separately to x, y, z

question: Evaluate lim(x→0) [(x+1)⁵−1]/x.
solution: Using the binomial expansion, (x+1)^5 = 1+5x+10x²+10x³+5x⁴+x⁵. So [(x+1)^5−1]/x = 5+10x+10x²+5x³+x⁴. As x→0, every term but the first vanishes, leaving the limit = 5.
steps: Subtract 1 and divide every term by x
Let x→0: only the constant term 5 survives

question: Find the derivative of f(x) = (x+1)/x (x≠0) using first principles.
steps: Compute f(x+h)−f(x) as a single fraction
Divide by h and take h→0: f′(x) = −1/x²

question: Find the mean and variance for the data: 6, 7, 10, 12, 13, 4, 8, 12.
solution: Mean = 72/8 = 9.0. Squared deviations from mean: computed per value, summing to give variance = 9.250 (using the formula Σ(xi−x̄)²/n).
steps: Compute (xi−mean)² for each value and sum

question: From the data of two series, Series A has mean 45, SD 6; Series B has mean 100, SD 8. Which series is more variable?
solution: Compare using Coefficient of Variation (CV) = (SD/mean)×100. For A: CV = (6/45)×100 ≈ 13.33%. For B: CV = (8/100)×100 = 8%. Since CV(A) > CV(B), Series A is more variable (relatively more spread out).
steps: Compute CV for each series separately
Higher CV means more variability → Series A is more variable

question: A die is thrown. Find the probability of getting a prime number.
solution: Prime numbers on a standard die (faces 1-6) are 2, 3, 5 — that's 3 favourable outcomes out of 6 total. P(prime) = 3/6 = 1/2.

question: From a group of 2 boys and 3 girls, two children are selected at random. Find the probability that at least one girl is selected.
solution: Total ways to choose 2 from 5 children: C(5,2) = 10. Ways with NO girl (both boys, but there are only 2 boys): C(2,2) = 1. P(no girl) = 1/10 = 1/10. P(at least one girl) = 1 − 1/10 = 9/10.
steps: P(at least one girl) = 1 − P(no girl) = 1 − 1/10 = 9/10

question: A box contains 10 red marbles, 20 blue marbles, and 30 green marbles. 5 marbles are drawn at random. Find the probability that exactly 2 are blue (describe the approach, assuming selection without replacement).
solution: Total marbles = 60, choose 5: C(60,5) ways total (the sample space). Favourable: choose exactly 2 blue from 20 blue marbles, C(20,2), and the remaining 3 from the other 40 (red+green) marbles, C(40,3). Probability = [C(20,2)×C(40,3)] / C(60,5).
steps: Total ways to draw 5 from 60: C(60,5)
Favourable: 2 from the 20 blue AND 3 from the other 40 non-blue
